_note: SOTA reference scores for capture ratios. Retrieved 2026-08-05/06 via web search of public leaderboards. Each entry records model, source, and as_of. NOTE the distinction the paper now draws in S5: the retrieval date is 2026-08-05/06 for every entry, but as_of -- the date the figure itself is current to -- ranges from 2024-10 (frozen tau-bench board) to 2026-08-06. CAVEAT: several figures come from leaderboard aggregator sites rather than the benchmark's own leaderboard page (marked primary: false); aggregators demonstrably disagree with each other (one listed WebArena at 95.6%, above the 78.24% human baseline). REVISED 2026-08-10: entries whose ceiling is not verified, same-split and primary-source are no longer printed in the paper at all -- Table 2 shows '---' for BFCL_v4_irrelevance, the three BFCL AST categories, GAIA and ALFWorld, and Figure 1 draws those rows floor-only. Their floors are 0.000-0.007 (or, for irrelevance, the metric's maximum, where the inversion is structural), so no ratio they could enter was ever load-bearing, which is the reason to drop the denominator rather than to footnote it. The two ceilings still printed and contested are tau-bench-airline (0.460 frozen board / 0.560 HAL, giving CR in [0.68, 0.83], Table 2 section-mark; the 0.700 aggregator figure is rejected, see that entry) and tau-bench-retail (frozen board, pilcrow marker, an upper bound on its CR).
_split_discipline: Each SOTA must be on the same split and metric as our floor: GPQA diamond (not main), tau-bench v1 original (not tau2-bench), WebArena original 812 tasks, SWE-bench Lite (not Verified/Full), GAIA validation, ALFWorld eval_out_of_distribution.

GPQA-diamond.source: Epoch AI GPQA Diamond benchmark page
GPQA-diamond.note: Diamond (n=198) chosen over main because essentially all published SOTA reports diamond; floor is 0.25 on either split.

GSM8K.note: Benchmark is effectively saturated; any value in 0.97-0.996 leaves the capture ratio at 0.03/0.15.

SWE-bench Lite.note: Floor is 0, so the capture ratio is 0 regardless of this figure.

GAIA.source: reported validation-set figures; the official GAIA validation leaderboard has been CLOSED, test-set leader is a system at 92.36%
GAIA.note: NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER as of 2026-08-10. Our floor is on validation; the validation board is closed, so no maintained same-split ceiling exists. Table 2 now shows '---' for SOTA and CR and reports headroom instead. Retained here only to record what was checked.

WebArena.source: leaderboard.steel.dev WebArena leaderboard, original 812-task set; human baseline 78.24%

BFCL_v4_irrelevance.source: LoopTool paper (arXiv:2511.09148) reporting BFCL-v3 Irrelevance; xLAM-2-70b-fc-r at 0.7891
BFCL_v4_irrelevance.note: LOAD-BEARING and the weakest-sourced entry: it is a v3 irrelevance figure, while our floor is measured on v4 files. NOTE the claim does not actually depend on it: the floor equals 1.0, which is the metric's maximum, so CR = 1/SOTA >= 1 for any model that is not perfect on the slice. RECHECKED 2026-08-06: no v4 irrelevance column is exposed by gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu (JS table, no per-category columns rendered), llm-stats bfcl-v4 (overall composite only, top 0.750 Qwen3.7 Max), or benchlm.ai. No same-split v4 ceiling exists to substitute. REVISED 2026-08-10: rather than print a cross-version ratio, the paper now shows '---' for this row's SOTA and CR and lets the structural statement (floor = the metric's maximum, so headroom is zero) carry it. This figure is retained only as the record of what was searched.

_BFCL_v4_composite_weights.quote: Non-Live Acc and Live Acc score calculation now excludes the Irrelevance/Relevance category scores.
_BFCL_v4_composite_weights.note: Sources the S5 claim that the irrelevance inversion propagates to the v4 headline ranking at 10% weight. Both halves of that sentence (excluded from the Live/Non-Live columns; 10% of the composite) are confirmed by this changelog entry. Cited as bfcl2025v4scoring.

BFCL_v4_simple_python.source: per-category AST columns not exposed by aggregators; BFCL v4 composite leader is Qwen3.7 Max at 0.750
BFCL_v4_simple_python.note: NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER as of 2026-08-10: model 'unresolved' means these are author estimates, and an estimate that cannot change a conclusion is one to delete rather than to footnote. Table 2 shows '---'. Read the per-category column off gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu/leaderboard.html (JS table) if an exact figure is ever wanted.

ALFWorld.source: recent ALFWorld agent papers; unseen/OOD split
ALFWorld.note: NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER as of 2026-08-10: sourced to agent papers rather than a maintained board (verified: false). Table 2 shows '---' and reports headroom (0.993 / 1.000) instead.

tau-bench-retail.note: The official board is frozen at the late-2024 model set. Newer models are reported mostly on tau2-bench, a different benchmark; using the frozen board keeps split and harness matched to our floor. If a newer same-split retail figure surfaces, it lowers this CR.

tau-bench-airline.agent: TAU-bench Tool Calling (the original v1 scaffold)
tau-bench-airline.leakage_cleanup: few-shot agent results removed 2025-12-08 for test-set examples in the demonstration file

rejected_2026_08_10.reason: PROVENANCE FAILURE, not a sourcing preference. The 0.700 airline score is reported in the same row as retail 0.862 and telecom 0.980. The telecom domain exists only in tau2-bench (arXiv:2506.07982), which ports airline and retail into a dual-control environment, so the row is a tau2-bench result relabelled by the aggregator; the same source records a prompt addendum to the airline agent policy. sota.json's own _split_discipline rule (tau-bench v1 original, not tau2-bench) forbids it. Earlier drafts kept it BECAUSE it was the most conservative available ceiling (CR 0.54); dropping it moves our headline number AGAINST our own conservatism, to CR 0.68.
rejected_2026_08_10.reusable_tell: a single row reporting airline + retail + telecom is tau2-bench, whatever the column header says

tau-bench-airline.note: Drives the airline capture ratio. Two ceilings are attributable to the original v1 harness: 0.460 (frozen official board) -> CR 0.83, and 0.560 (HAL, original Tool Calling scaffold, leakage-cleaned Dec 2025) -> CR 0.68. We quote 0.560 because it is the best-documented same-harness figure, and state CR in [0.68, 0.83] wherever the number carries argumentative weight. Cited in-text as hal2025taubench; appendix C.6(i) sets out the exclusion above.
